I farm only 7 mu, but I have been doing this for 40 years, I know my land, and I have well irrigation, so I would run a steady wheat-maize rotation rather than gamble on anything complicated. Because some people in my household work off-farm, I would keep the plan simple, timely, and labor-efficient. For wheat, I would use improved seed, prepare a decent seedbed with rotary tillage, push nitrogen enough for stable yield, and rely on three irrigations because water is available and wheat here responds well to it. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed, reduce tillage pressure after wheat harvest by going no-tillage, and keep fertilizer and water at a medium-high level so the crop can make full use of the summer season. I would not chase extreme input levels; I would aim for stable output, manageable labor, and low risk.
